captures.q: What are the arguments in “The Upstream Unfoldings: Six Operable Transforms from Sappho 31 into the Apocalypse's Channel — revelationfirst.com/upstream/” by Lee Sharks? Ground your answer in a reading of the text itself.
captures.description: THE SIX PLATES READ FROM THE SITE, THEIR GRADES KEPT, THE SCORE AND ITS FAILURES CARRIED: asked for the arguments of The Upstream Unfoldings, grounded in the text, ChatGPT reads the live surface the deposit records (Revelation First ×12; the author's blog ×1 for the frozen clauses) plate by plate under the page's own grades: Longinus (Peri Hypsous 10.1–3, the quotation cut at the sixteenth line) and Philo ('the suppression signature') attested; Addition D and AJ 11.234–241, and BJ 1.436–444 with ἀναζωπυρέω, tested; the Slavonic carrier contested and carried openly; Revelation 12 tested under seal, eight of nine with C6 at double weight, C1 failing, the birth-cry covered by Isaiah 26:17, the fire-lexeme missing. It sets out T's seven stations, quotes the Logos sentence from 'Sappho, Mother of the Logos' ('a voice that survives its flesh by becoming an inscription that constitutes its receiver'), and closes on the page's own limit, that it 'does not assert authorship, influence in the biographical sense, or the identification sentence.' Six image cards, one per plate, the first of them a page on Sappho Fragment 16, not 31.

atoms.evidence: The argument of Lee Sharks’s The Upstream Unfoldings
The Upstream Unfoldings is an attempt to turn comparative literary interpretation
But he explicitly says that it does not assert authorship, influence in the biographical sense, or the identification sentence.
The pivotal idea appears in the page's linked argument, “Sappho, Mother of the Logos.”

Sappho’s Fragment 31 contains a repeatable literary structure that can be traced through ancient Greek and Jewish literature into Revelation 12. He calls this structure an “executable relational apparatus,”
But he explicitly says that it does not assert authorship, influence in the biographical sense, or the identification sentence.
Sharks begins with On the Sublime 10.1–3, where Longinus quotes Sappho’s Fragment 31.
